objections.claim: The protected verifier closure still excludes its invoking GitHub workflow. A PR can modify the required-check workflow to skip base-tree materialization and the VERIFIER_CLOSURE_DIGEST check, then emit the expected successful check; requiring PRs and forbidding direct pushes does not prevent this PR-mediated bypass, and the merge controller only observes the resulting green status. The invocation path must be independently protected—such as an out-of-tree required workflow—and tested with a workflow-only bypass fixture. Candidate sha256:f1a1e91ba6a6b4fa043dc68669a029dbad49caaac169c9c2ec9c76e88a3a6779.

The initial hardened-verifier deployment is circular. At fc0fa05, the trusted base copy cannot recognize verifier-closure changes, protected-root variables, or Eye-signed authority transitions, so it cannot enforce the rule required to admit its own successor. Tests that assume the hardened verifier is already the base do not establish a safe genesis transition. The approach needs an explicit out-of-tree bootstrap verifier and provisioning ceremony that validates the first closure, roots, workflow, and Eye signature before the E2 merge.

Typed evidence is still not bound semantically to the readiness item it purports to discharge. Any passing run-oracles entry or green check run at the release SHA can be referenced by an unrelated P0 item; executing it and checking its SHA proves only that check's own claim, contrary to the frozen rule that green CI alone is not proof of operability. Each item needs a closed evidence contract binding item_id and required claim to permitted oracle/check/artifact semantics, plus a negative fixture proving that swapping valid evidence between unrelated items fails.

Blanket exclusion of docs/runs/ violates the frozen mandate to reconcile every tracked Node-version documentation claim and relies on directory location as a normativity decision. That tree contains active workshop and authority artifacts as well as historical evidence. The oracle must scan all tracked text and require an authenticated historical/non-governing disposition for immutable legacy claims, or route an actual incompatibility with frozen artifacts as plan-escalation; a false-positive-only inventory and directory exclusion do not discharge the mandate.
